name: TrustDemoDataElements
title: Data elements of the journeys
description: Every data element of the data dictionary, by its code (TD.<data set>.DE<nn>).

concept.definition: The child's name as the birth hospital records it.
The child's date of birth.
The parent or guardian, for a subject with no identity document such as a newborn (STT-PAY-005).
The birth hospital's own identifier for the child. It is not carried in the DVC.
The product given, in the issuer's product coding (illustrative PreQual-style codes).
The date the dose was given. The hospital record holds the time as well; the DVC carries the date.
The batch (lot) of the vaccine given.
The dose's number in its series. Recorded by the hospital; the minimal DVC payload does not carry it.
The clinician who gave or supervised the dose.
The trust-network participant whose key signs the DVC (J1: XXR).
When the DVC was signed.
When the DVC stops verifying, where the issuer sets an expiry.
Identifies the document signer certificate on the trust list that verifies the DVC (J1: 916ffa567c0f44a2).
The household on the CHW's roster that the child joins.
The child's given name.
The child's family name.
The child's date of birth.
The country the child was born in, when abroad.
Whether the family holds vaccination cards from abroad.
The id the child carries until civil registration catches up.
The community health worker who registered the child.
When the registration was captured, on the phone, possibly offline.
The family member who gave the answers.

concept.display: Dose read from a foreign card
concept.definition: One dose read from a foreign DVC with the unverified triage read (STT-VER-011), saved as reported by the family.
The issuer's product code as read from the card; no national code is added yet.
The date of vaccination as read from the card.
The batch number as read from the card.
The family member who showed the card: the dose's information source.
Always reported-unverified for a triage read (decision table TD.DT.01); recorded as primarySource false with a note.
The child referred.
The community health worker who made the referral.
The clinic that will verify the cards.
When the referral was made.
Why the child is referred: unverified foreign vaccination cards.
The reported doses the clinic is asked to verify.
Active until the clinic records an outcome for every dose it lists, then completed (indicator TD.IND.03).
The kid of the DVC verified, which names the signer's certificate.
The participant that signed the DVC (CWT iss).
When the verification ran.
The system that verified the DVC.
The library's typed result (STT-VER-008).
The step at which verification stopped, when it failed.
Why verification stopped, when it failed: the input of decision table TD.DT.01.
When the verifier last refreshed its cached copy of the trust list; a signer added since then fails with KidNotFound (STT-VER-006).
What the DVC becomes in the record (decision table TD.DT.01).
The dose recorded from the verified DVC.
The reported dose the verified one replaces.
The trust framework the DVC was verified under.
The vaccine code as the issuer signed it; kept, never replaced (STD-SEM-001).
The national schedule's antigen-and-dose code, added beside the product code. Absent for an unmapped dose, which the TrustDemoOnesaImmunization profile (onesaEpi 1..1) does not yet represent.
How the schedule code was found (decision table TD.DT.02).
The clinician who confirmed an equivalent the map did not cover.
Whether the schedule counts the dose (decision table TD.DT.03): only doses from a primary source with a national schedule code.
A dose of the national schedule the evaluation finds due (decision table TD.DT.04).
The schedule's antigen-and-dose code of the dose due.
The forecast for the dose.
The child's date of birth plus the schedule action's timing age.
The reminder created for the next visit.
The family member whose summary is shared.
The person who shares the link and decides who may open it.
The home-country service that hosts the record and checks every request.
The patient summary the link releases.
The first day the link may be opened.
The expiry the holder chose; after it the link releases nothing (STD-ACC-001).
The purpose of use the holder allows (J4: treatment).
Whether the holder protected the link with a passcode. The passcode itself is never stored in the record.
When the holder withdrew the link, if they did.
When the request arrived.
The receiving system abroad that asked for the manifest.
Where the request came from.
The home-country gateway that answered and logged the request.
Whose record was asked for.
Whether the manifest was released (decision table TD.DT.05).
0 when released; 4 (minor failure) when refused.
Why nothing was released, when refused.
The holder's consent the request was checked against.
The summary released, when released.
